content:
Problem Phishing detectors usually return a bare label. Analysts also need to know why an email was flagged.
Approach Each email goes through three parts, and the Streamlit demo shows all three results side by side:
Fine-tuned classifier: Qwen3-14B fine-tuned with QLoRA makes the phishing / legitimate decision. RAG: retrieves relevant threat intelligence from APWG reports and MITRE ATT&CK. Chain-of-Thought module: produces a JSON report with a risk score, indicators and analysis. The model is exported to GGUF for local inference with Ollama.
Data: 4,000 emails from the Human-LLM Generated Phishing-Legitimate Emails dataset on Kaggle, 1,000 each of human-written and LLM-written phishing and legitimate emails, split 80/10/10.
Results On the 400-email test set:
Metric Baseline Fine-tuned 14B Fine-tuned 27B Accuracy 50% 88.75% 99.0% Precision 0.500 0.833 0.980 Recall 1.000 0.970 1.000 F1 0.667 0.896 0.990 Adding RAG did not improve classification accuracy. Its value is giving each verdict interpretable threat-intel sources.
summary: Fine-tuned Qwen3-14B with QLoRA to classify phishing emails, plus threat-intel RAG and Chain-of-Thought analysis in a Streamlit demo.
title: LLM-Based Phishing Email Detection

content:
Problem Does retrieval actually help a local open-weight model on a domain exam, and is it better than putting the whole study guide in the prompt?
Approach Benchmark: the 2026 entry-level iPAS Net Zero Planning Manager exam, 198 multiple-choice questions. Knowledge base: 1,245 chunks from 24 laws, the 2025 iPAS study guides and Ministry of Environment GHG documents. Retrieval: compared BM25, dense (bge-m3), hybrid (RRF) and hybrid with a bge-reranker-v2-m3 reranker, across three query formats. Answering: three Qwen models via Ollama, each tested closed-book, with RAG, and with the full study guide in the prompt. Significance is tested with McNemar’s test. Results Model Closed-book RAG Full guide in prompt RAG vs. closed-book qwen3:8b 80.8% 88.4% 86.4% p = 0.006 qwen3:14b 85.4% 91.4% 88.4% p = 0.004 qwen3.5:27b 89.9% 94.4% 91.4% p = 0.078 RAG beat both closed-book and full-guide prompting for every model. Hybrid retrieval with reranking reached Hit@5 = 0.938. Error analysis shows most remaining RAG errors come from questions whose answer is not in the knowledge base, not from retrieval misses. Limitations: retrieval labels are model-judged, and the study covers one prompt and one exam year.
summary: RAG evaluation on Taiwan’s iPAS Net Zero Planning Manager exam with local open-weight models: closed-book vs. RAG vs. the full study guide in the prompt.
title: NetZero-RAG

content: Approach Built a CLIP baseline classifier and a CLIP + LoRA variant for parameter-efficient fine-tuning. Trained and evaluated on FaceForensics++ (C40), with real YouTube videos against FaceSwap and NeuralTextures fakes. Evaluated at both frame level and video level, with ROC curves and a script that visualizes misclassified samples. Results Model Level AUC ACC F1 Baseline Frame 0.634 0.793 0.881 Baseline Video 0.651 0.782 0.874 LoRA Frame 0.803 0.884 0.936 LoRA Video 0.806 0.891 0.940 Pretrained weights are available in the repository’s releases.
summary: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning of CLIP for deepfake detection on FaceForensics++, evaluated at frame and video level.
title: Deepfake Detection with CLIP + LoRA
